description: Internalize claude-auto-retry (~600 LoC) into cam-cli as src/retry/* and ship cam claude/retry-monitor subcommands so the external dependency can be dropped.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Bun.spawn supports stdio: 'inherit'/'pipe'/'ignore', detached, env, proc.pid, proc.kill('SIGTERM'), proc.exited Promise, proc.unref(). ipc and terminal (PTY) available. spawnSync ~60% faster than Node. No breaking changes affect this port.
Bun.TOML.parse is GA in current Bun and parses TOML v1.0 strings into JS objects; throws on invalid input. Used in US-002 for retry config.
Bun.$ tagged-template shell with .text()/.json()/.quiet() helpers; replaces node:child_process.execFile for tmux invocations. Used in US-003 for tmux.ts.
Bun.file(path) returns a BunFile; Bun.write(path, data) creates parents on demand — preferred over node:fs per project CLAUDE.md. Used in US-002 for config and logger.

userStories.title: Port patterns.ts + time-parser.ts with tests and license attribution
userStories.description: As a cam-cli maintainer, I need the pure detection/parsing primitives from claude-auto-retry ported to TypeScript under src/retry/ so subsequent stories can build the config, logger, monitor, and launcher on top of typed, tested helpers.
acceptanceCriteria: src/retry/patterns.ts exports the same rate-limit / usage-limit detection patterns and helpers as the original patterns.js, with explicit TypeScript types on all exports.

src/retry/time-parser.ts exports the same parsing functions as the original time-parser.js, with explicit TypeScript types and the same semantics for absolute times, relative durations, and 'tomorrow X' shapes.
Both ported files carry the MIT attribution header (claude-auto-retry v0.2.2, cheapestinference contributors, Eduardo Caminha port).
LICENSES/claude-auto-retry-MIT.txt exists with the verbatim original MIT license text.
test/retry/patterns.test.ts covers every exported matcher with positive + negative cases derived from the original behavior.
test/retry/time-parser.test.ts covers absolute, relative, and 'tomorrow' shapes plus invalid input handling.
No new runtime dependencies are added to package.json for these two modules.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Source: /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/claude-auto-retry/src/patterns.js and time-parser.js. New files: src/retry/patterns.ts, src/retry/time-parser.ts, test/retry/patterns.test.ts, test/retry/time-parser.test.ts, LICENSES/claude-auto-retry-MIT.txt. Pure functions only — no Bun APIs, no filesystem, no spawn. Keep exported function names identical to the originals so later ports can import 1:1. Use `import { test, expect } from "bun:test"`.

userStories.title: Port config.ts + logger.ts with cam-namespaced paths
userStories.description: As a cam-cli user, I need retry config and logs to live under cam-cli's own namespace (~/.config/cam/retry.toml and ~/.cam/retry-logs/) so cam-cli does not collide with or depend on claude-auto-retry's filesystem layout.
acceptanceCriteria: src/retry/config.ts loads/validates TOML config from ~/.config/cam/retry.toml (expanded from $HOME), creating the file with documented defaults on first read if it does not exist.

src/retry/config.ts uses `Bun.TOML.parse` (not a hand-rolled parser, not a third-party TOML package). On parse failure, surface a clear error including the file path and the parser's exception message.
src/retry/logger.ts writes structured logs under ~/.cam/retry-logs/ with the same log levels and rotation behavior as the original logger.js.
Both ported files carry the MIT attribution header.
Config schema is fully typed (no `any`); invalid TOML fields surface a clear error rather than crashing the process.
test/retry/config.test.ts covers default-creation, parse success, parse failure, and path expansion using a temp $HOME (e.g. process.env.HOME override).
test/retry/logger.test.ts covers log file creation, append behavior, and that the directory is created on demand, using a temp $HOME.
Tests do not write to the real ~/.config/cam or ~/.cam — they isolate via $HOME or an injected base dir.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Source: /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/claude-auto-retry/src/config.js and logger.js. New files: src/retry/config.ts, src/retry/logger.ts, test/retry/config.test.ts, test/retry/logger.test.ts. TOML parsing: use `Bun.TOML.parse` (GA in current Bun) — no hand-rolled parser, no third-party TOML package. File I/O: prefer `Bun.file` and `Bun.write` over node:fs per project CLAUDE.md. Make the base dir injectable so tests can pass a temp dir without monkey-patching globals.

userStories.title: Port tmux.ts + monitor.ts with processOneTick adapter for tests
userStories.description: As a cam-cli maintainer, I need the tmux capture wrapper and the monitor loop ported with a single testable tick function so the rate-limit detection / sleep / resume cycle can be unit-tested without spawning real tmux or sleeping in wall-clock time.
acceptanceCriteria: src/retry/tmux.ts wraps `tmux capture-pane`-style invocations via `Bun.$` (per project CLAUDE.md) and exports typed helpers matching the original tmux.js surface.
src/retry/monitor.ts exposes a `processOneTick(deps)` function whose dependencies (current time, tmux capture, sleep, logger, config) are injected, so tests can drive a full cycle synchronously.
The default exported monitor entrypoint composes `processOneTick` with real Bun-backed adapters and preserves the original monitor.js end-to-end behavior.
Both ported files carry the MIT attribution header.

test/retry/monitor.test.ts drives processOneTick through: (a) no-limit-detected, (b) rate-limit-detected with future resume time, (c) resume-time-reached → resume signaled, using fake clock + fake tmux output.
test/retry/tmux.test.ts covers the parsing/shaping of capture output with fixture strings (no real tmux process spawned).
No test spawns a real tmux session, real sleep > 100ms, or real claude process.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Source: /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/claude-auto-retry/src/tmux.js and monitor.js. New files: src/retry/tmux.ts, src/retry/monitor.ts, test/retry/tmux.test.ts, test/retry/monitor.test.ts. Depends on US-001 (patterns, time-parser) and US-002 (config, logger). The `processOneTick` shape is the key testability requirement called out in the issue spec — keep deps as a single object param so future stories can inject more without breaking signatures.

userStories.title: Implement launcher.ts and cam claude subcommand (print mode)
userStories.description: As a cam-cli user, I need a `cam claude` subcommand that launches Claude in print mode under the retry launcher so that non-interactive runs (used by run/next/plan) automatically survive rate limits without requiring the external claude-auto-retry binary.
acceptanceCriteria: src/retry/launcher.ts exports a `launchClaude(opts)` function that spawns `claude` via `Bun.spawn` with `stdio: 'inherit'` for print mode, forwards args, env, and cwd, and applies the retry/resume policy on rate-limit exit.
launcher.ts does NOT call `createTmuxSession` — the issue spec explicitly skips that path; interactive/tmux mode is handled separately in US-005.
launcher.ts carries the MIT attribution header.
index.ts (or src/commands/claude.ts) registers a `cam claude [args...]` subcommand that delegates to `launchClaude` in print mode and forwards exit code.
`cam claude --help` prints usage including which flags are forwarded to claude vs. consumed by cam.
The subcommand does NOT register a `--permission-mode` flag (enforced by test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts).

cam claude does not parse the forwarded argv beyond consuming a leading `--help`. All other args are passed verbatim to the child `claude` process so callers can use any claude flag (including `--permission-mode`) without cam needing to know it. Unit test asserts that `cam claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions /cam-next` reaches the spawn adapter with argv `[claude, --permission-mode, bypassPermissions, /cam-next]`.
test/retry/launcher.test.ts uses an injectable spawn adapter to verify args forwarding, exit-code propagation, and the rate-limit → wait → retry path without spawning real claude.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Source: /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/claude-auto-retry/src/launcher.js. New files: src/retry/launcher.ts, src/commands/claude.ts (or wire directly in index.ts — check existing convention in src/commands/init.ts and src/commands/setup.ts), test/retry/launcher.test.ts. Gotcha: `index.ts` and `src/commands/` are scanned by test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts — do NOT add `--permission-mode`. Use `Bun.spawn({ stdio: ['inherit','inherit','inherit'] })` and `await proc.exited`. Make the spawn function injectable so tests can stub it.

userStories.title: Implement interactive mode with monitor fork and cam retry-monitor internal subcommand
userStories.description: As a cam-cli user running an interactive Claude session, I need cam claude to fork a background monitor process that watches the session via tmux and resumes on rate-limit clear, so interactive sessions get the same auto-retry behavior the external tool provided.
acceptanceCriteria: When `cam claude` is invoked with `$TMUX` env var set (i.e. running inside a tmux session) AND args do not include `-p`/`--print`, it forks a detached `cam retry-monitor <pane> <pid>` child via `Bun.spawn({ detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' })` and `proc.unref()`.

When `cam claude` is invoked outside tmux (`$TMUX` unset) AND without `-p`/`--print`, the subcommand exits non-zero with an error message pointing the user at `cam run` (which provides the tmux session). Unit test covers this error path.
`cam retry-monitor` is registered as an internal subcommand (not advertised in top-level help unless `--help` is passed to it directly) that runs the monitor.ts loop against the given pane/pid.
The monitor child writes its PID to a discoverable location (see US-006) and logs to ~/.cam/retry-logs/ via logger.ts.

The launcher installs SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers that propagate to the child claude process and trigger monitor PID-file cleanup; SIGWINCH is forwarded for terminal resize. Unit test mocks `process.on('SIGINT')` and asserts the handler signals the child and calls the cleanup function.

test/retry/interactive.test.ts (or extends launcher.test.ts) verifies the fork path via an injectable spawn adapter: confirms detached/ignore/unref flags are set and the child argv is `[bun-or-self, ..., 'retry-monitor', pane, pid]`.
The subcommand does NOT register a `--permission-mode` flag.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Builds on US-003 (monitor.processOneTick) and US-004 (launcher). Files: src/retry/launcher.ts (extend), src/commands/retry-monitor.ts, register subcommand in index.ts. Use `Bun.spawn({ detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' })` per Bun docs (officialDocsConsulted entry). Routing key: `$TMUX` env var (NOT TTY check) AND absence of `-p`/`--print` in argv. The 'internal' nature means retry-monitor should still respond to --help but should not be listed in the top-level command index. Coordinate the pane/pid contract with US-006's PID file convention.

userStories.title: Switchover: route internal claude spawns through cam claude and add retry-pid helpers
userStories.description: As a cam-cli maintainer, I need run/next/plan to invoke the in-process retry launcher (or `cam claude`) instead of the external `claude-auto-retry` binary, and a small src/util/retry-pid.ts helper to track monitor PIDs, so the internal port becomes the live code path.
acceptanceCriteria: src/util/retry-pid.ts exports helpers to (a) write a monitor PID file at ~/.cam/retry.pid, (b) read it, (c) check liveness via `process.kill(pid, 0)`, (d) remove it on shutdown.

All cam-cli code paths that currently spawn `claude-auto-retry` (in src/commands/run.ts, src/commands/next.ts, src/commands/plan.ts and any helper) are rerouted to invoke the internal launcher (`launchClaude` from US-004) or `cam claude` subprocess.
Existing tests for run/next/plan still pass (or are updated to assert the new internal launcher is called).

No remaining `claude-auto-retry` string literal in `src/commands/run.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`, or `src/commands/plan.ts` (the rerouted launcher paths). Wider scrub of `init.ts`, `resume.ts`, `index.ts` HELP strings, embedded vendor, and tests is US-007's scope.
test/retry/retry-pid.test.ts covers write/read/liveness/remove with a temp dir.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: New file: src/util/retry-pid.ts, test/retry/retry-pid.test.ts. Edits: src/commands/run.ts, src/commands/next.ts, src/commands/plan.ts (verify via `grep -r claude-auto-retry src/commands/`). PID file path is ~/.cam/retry.pid (single file convention used by US-007's resume.ts rewire). Use `process.kill(pid, 0)` for liveness (does not actually signal — throws ESRCH if dead). Do not yet remove the external-dep checks in init.ts / resume.ts — that is US-007's scope.
